title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation of Observer Error-Rates Using the EM Algorithm
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C (Applied Statistics)
summary: Introduces the latent-class model in which each observer has an unknown class-confusion matrix and the true class of each item is latent, and shows that EM yields maximum-likelihood estimates of observer error rates and true classes without gold labels (motivated by compiling patient records from several clinicians).
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's anchored cell model is a Dawid-Skene descendant: models are observers, cells are items. SpecDx differs in three ways: the truth is a set (A_c in {{x},{x,y},empty}), the specification's declared value is treated as one more fallible rater (the anchor), and per-model accuracy is parameterised by ability minus cell difficulty instead of a free confusion matrix per rater.
baseline_notes: Run crowd-kit DawidSkene on a long table (task=cell id, worker=model id plus a pseudo-worker 'spec' carrying d_c, label=read value). Flag cells whose posterior truth differs from d_c as hidden-requirement or mis-key candidates. It cannot output a two-value truth or an empty truth, so ambiguity and contradiction are invisible to it, and it treats the specification as an ordinary worker. Offline, pip install crowd-kit.

relation_to_specdx: GLAD's accuracy term (labeler ability times inverse item difficulty inside a logistic) is the direct ancestor of SpecDx's sigma(alpha_m - beta_g) faithful-reading probability. GLAD assumes one true label per item and has no anchor rater or empty or two-valued truth.

It is a direct ablation of SpecDx without set-valued truth and without the anchor. Runs offline.

title: Learning From Crowds
venue: Journal of Machine Learning Research
summary: Gives a probabilistic EM approach for supervised learning from several annotators' noisy labels without a gold standard, jointly estimating annotator quality, the hidden true labels and a classifier, and outperforming majority voting.
relation_to_specdx: It is the canonical learning-from-crowds model. SpecDx shares the joint estimation of rater quality and latent truth, but it has no features or classifier, because the items are specification cells and the truth may be a set.

title: Learning Whom to Trust with MACE
venue: Proceedings of the 2013 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies
summary: MACE (Multi-Annotator Competence Estimation) learns without supervision which annotators are trustworthy and predicts the underlying labels, improving both label accuracy and trustworthiness estimates over standard baselines (from the S2 TLDR and metadata; the abstract was not available).
relation_to_specdx: It is the closest classic analogue of SpecDx's competent-reading-or-noise mixture for each rater. SpecDx adds item difficulty, set-valued truth and an anchor, and restricts errors to values outside the entailment set.

title: Bayesian Classifier Combination
venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2012), PMLR 22
summary: Develops Bayesian classifier combination: a framework that models each base classifier's or human assessor's output given the unknown true label, starting from Dawid-Skene and adding richer structure via MCMC. It needs neither probabilistic nor independent base models, nor a correct one, and gives interpretable diagnostics.
relation_to_specdx: It is the Bayesian Dawid-Skene (IBCC) that SpecDx's MAP/EM fit with Dirichlet priors resembles. IBCC has no anchor rater, no item difficulty and no set-valued truth.

  abstract = 	 {Bayesian model averaging linearly mixes the probabilistic predictions of multiple models, each weighted by its posterior probability. This is the coherent Bayesian way of combining multiple models only under certain restrictive assumptions, which we outline. We explore a general framework for Bayesian model combination (which differs from model averaging) in the context of classification. This framework explicitly models the relationship between each model’s output and the unknown true label. The framework does not require that the models be probabilistic (they can even be human assessors), that they share prior information or receive the same training data, or that they be independent in their errors. bibtex: @InProceedings{pmlr-v267-goel25b, title = {Great Models Think Alike and this Undermines {AI} Oversight}, author = {Goel, Shashwat and Str\"{u}ber, Joschka and Auzina, Ilze Amanda and Chandra, Karuna K and Kumaraguru, Ponnurangam and Kiela, Douwe and Prabhu, Ameya and Bethge, Matthias and Geiping, Jonas}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning}, pages = {19621--19678}, year = {2025}, editor = {Singh, Aarti and Fazel, Maryam and Hsu, Daniel and Lacoste-Julien, Simon and Berkenkamp, Felix and Maharaj, Tegan and Wagstaff, Kiri and Zhu, Jerry}, volume = {267}, series = {Proceedings of Machine Learning Research}, month = {13--19 Jul}, publisher = {PMLR}, pdf = {https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v267/main/assets/goel25b/goel25b.pdf}, url = {https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/goel25b.html}, abstract = {As Language Model (LM) capabilities advance, evaluating and supervising them at scale is getting harder for humans. title: Validating LLM-as-a-Judge Systems under Rating Indeterminacy
venue: arXiv
summary: Introduces 'rating indeterminacy', where rating criteria admit several valid interpretations so a rater may deem multiple ratings correct. Gives a framework for validating LLM judges under it and shows that forced-choice elicitation and aggregation can heavily bias judge validation (NeurIPS 2025 per the arXiv comment).
relation_to_specdx: Rating indeterminacy is SpecDx's ambiguity defect (A_c = {x, y}) viewed from the evaluation side. It supports eliciting or modelling set-valued truth rather than forcing one label.

title: Are LLMs Better than Reported? Detecting Label Errors and Mitigating Their Effect on Model Performance
venue: arXiv
summary: Uses an ensemble of LLMs as judges to flag likely mislabeled examples in four TRUE factual-consistency datasets and SummEval. It compares expert, crowd and LLM annotation, and finds substantial label errors whose correction changes reported model performance.
relation_to_specdx: An LLM committee auditing a dataset's given labels (a fallible anchor) is SpecDx's setting restricted to static labels. Its confidence-thresholded ensemble vote is a simple baseline for SpecDx's mis-key detection.
